elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 7.2(e): "The Issuer, as the customer under this Agreement, may, for convenience and without cause, remove the Servicer and terminate the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement..." There are no Order Forms in this structure, and Section 8.3 makes Agreement-level termination an exhaustive, event-driven mechanic; the operative insertion nonetheless gives the customer side an unconditional at-will right to end the Servicer's engagement under this Agreement, which is the vendor-facing service relationship the rule targets. The deterministic flag "Customer convenience termination present: false" reflects only that the text does not literally read "terminate this Agreement for convenience"; in substance an unconditional Customer election to end the servicing engagement is a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2(e): "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer" — exactly 30 days, written, no additional conditions (no Successor Servicer acceptance condition; Section 7.3 fixes effectiveness at "the date stated in the notice of termination").

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2(e): "the Servicer will refund, pro rata, any Servicing Fees paid in advance for any period after the effective date of the termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period), and Servicing Fees are the fees payable to the Vendor under this Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1 No Resignation: "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement." Resignation is barred except on legal inability — a cause/impossibility trigger, not convenience — and no other Vendor at-will exit appears in the cited termination architecture (Section 7.2 removal is Customer/Indenture-Trustee side; Section 8.3 triggers are event-based). Element already met and correctly left untouched.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on "thirty (30) days' prior written notice," which is outside the literal 60–90 day band. This is a deliberate overshoot in the Customer's favour at the preferred level and is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the retained text nor Section 7.2(e) imposes any early-termination fee, penalty, make-whole or instalment on the Customer for the convenience removal (the Section 8.1/8.2 Make-Whole Payment attaches to Certificateholder redemption options, not to this right), so there is no fee to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori: Section 7.1 bars Servicer resignation altogether except on legal inability, so the Vendor has no convenience exit at any time, let alone mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no Vendor convenience termination right to which a notice period could attach (Section 7.1 No Resignation).

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted Section 7.2(e) supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and the pro rata prepaid-fee refund, and retained Section 7.1 already denies the Servicer any convenience exit.

The deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" miss is a wording artefact, not a substantive gap: the insertion terminates the Servicer's rights and obligations under the Agreement at the Issuer's unconditional election, which is the vendor-side exit the rule protects. Terminating the whole Agreement was not available without contradicting the exhaustive Section 8.3 triggers, so the targeted removal is the correct implementation.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletions, no re-drafting of Sections 7.1, 7.2(c)-(d), 7.3 or 8.3, and none of the usual model-language extras (no "in whole or in part" surplus, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural add-ons). The apposition "as the customer under this Agreement" is descriptive filler that could be trimmed ("customer" is not a defined term here), but it imposes no obligation and does not create a dangling reference.

Intent preserved: Section 7.3 already fixes effectiveness at "the date stated in the notice of termination" for any termination, so the 30-day notice operates without conflict; the Section 7.2(c) Cellco reassumption is drafted to fire on any "removal ... pursuant to this Section 7.2" and therefore engages consistently and in the Customer's favour; Section 8.3's Agreement-level triggers are untouched.

Residual point to confirm outside the four elements (not a checklist defect): Section 7.4's Successor Servicer machinery and the Indenture's covenants were not supplied in full, so the drafter should verify that a removal initiated by the Issuer rather than the Indenture Trustee does not require conforming language in Section 7.4(a)(i) or Rating Agency/Indenture Trustee notice, to avoid a later argument that the new right is inoperative.
